info.title: Review E5 cartogram, check E6/E7 impact

opencode2.text:
You are a subagent spawned by another session.
Project: Sheridan Datathon 2026, Tangerine track. Repo: /Users/ajeet/Projects/Hackathons/Sheridan Datathon 2026 (React 19 + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind, Python pipeline under scripts/engine with uv, vitest, pytest). Sunday 02:30 AM, code freeze 9:00 AM today.

TASK: review E5 Storm Atlas with its newly added features, then check whether E6 (judge mode) and E7 (Solana receipts) need any fixes as a result of the E5 changes. This is review only: append your findings to docs/reviews.md, do not fix anything yourself.

WHAT TO REVIEW (the E5 surface as it now stands):

1. Commit f058bdd "E5 Storm Atlas with verdict-band fold, strip plot drill-down, and bank-wide scenario mode" — the original E5: StormAtlas.tsx five-band cell grid, AtlasSection.tsx (headline, baseline vs shocked scenario summaries), AtlasStripPlot.tsx + src/lib/atlasPlot.ts strip plot drill-down, stormAtlas.ts reworked to the five verdict bands, atlas.css.

2. Commit ac6b652 "atlas.json district precompute on the five verdict bands" — scripts/engine/atlas.py (district/account join, band_for_runway port of verdict.ts branch order, baseline plus 4 scenario passes), test_atlas.py, build.py emit, verify.py atlas gate (ATLAS_BANDS), regenerated public/data/engine/atlas.json, correction entry in docs/decisions.md. NOTE: this commit deleted scripts/engine/weather_state.py and weather_state_goldens.json per a user decision retiring the seven-state ladder; the ONLY vocabulary is src/lib/verdict.ts five bands (critical, storm_warning, watch, fair_skies, clear).

3. Commit f5cb657 "district storm cartogram and population rain gauge" — src/lib/atlasData.ts strict loader (accepts band list under verdict_bands or states key), Cartogram.tsx (77 tiles, region bands, severity = critical+storm_warning share, 5 bins, no_data hatch keeping account counts), RainGauge.tsx (fill = share outside critical+storm_warning, 80% reference line), AtlasSection.tsx mount (ax-lead grid: StormAtlas beside gauge, cartogram section, strip plot), atlas.css additions.

REVIEW FOCUS for E5:
- Correctness: does the cartogram severity math match its printed legend? Do baseline/scenario table selection and the scenarioLabel contract hold? Does the no_data hatch render honestly (district 69 has real account data, only demographic cells missing)? Does the gauge reading match its face print?
- Parity/honesty: UI reads counts, never recomputes; legends print definitions; region-not-geography caveat present; reduced motion double-gated.
- Python side: band_for_runway branch order vs src/lib/verdict.ts (the two special states decided before thresholds); determinism; verify.py gate vocabulary-agnostic sums; test coverage of the 5 bands and boundaries (deci 9/10/29/30/59/60/119/120, buffer_depleted, no_shortfall).
- Loader strictness: atlasData refusal messages, sum invariants, key acceptance (verdict_bands vs states).
- Any place where the RETIRED seven-state vocabulary (cloudy, overcast, rain, drought, storm, flood as state keys) still leaks into shipped code or artifacts. Note: src/index.css --rv-drought tokens are pre-pivot Money River machinery (unmounted, historical), and docs/research.md exploratory tables are history; flag only if retired names appear in LIVE surfaces or artifacts.

CROSS-IMPACT CHECKS (E6 and E7 as a result of E5 changes):
- E6 (commit 4d9ff25: judgeMode.ts single key table, GuardChips, RehearsalDock, useEdgeGuard, useJudgeShortcuts, rehearsal.ts, public/judge-sheet.html, consoleStore key map integration): does anything in E6 assume the old seven-state vocabulary, the deleted weatherState.ts, or the pre-fold stormAtlas API? Does E6's N-key safe account pool or edge guards interact badly with the new atlas scenario routing (AtlasSection now loads atlas.json and picks baseline vs scenario tables)?
- E7 (Solana receipts, currently UNCOMMITTED in the working tree: src/data/receipts.ts, src/components/console/ReceiptStamp.tsx + test, BaselineCard.tsx mount, src/index.css receipt styles, src/dashScan.test.ts entries, public/data/memo-devnet*.json, scripts/solana/evidence/*): does the E5 cartogram or atlas loader collide with receipts.ts loading patterns? Does dashScan.test.ts (modified by both E7 and earlier E5 work) still scan a complete file set? Does BaselineCard's new ReceiptStamp render break any E5 or console test? Is the uncommitted E7 set internally consistent (all files present for the tests it references)?
- Also verify the full current suite is actually green: run npm run typecheck, npx vitest run, uv run pytest -q, uv run python -m scripts.engine.verify. Report exact numbers. If anything fails, that is a finding.

APPEND your review to docs/reviews.md with a dated heading "## Nov 08 2026, E5 review: cartogram, gauge, atlas precompute (plus E6/E7 impact check)" following the existing file's format (verdict PASS/FAIL, severity table with file:line, verified clean paragraph, non-blocking notes, recurring patterns). The file has a concurrent uncommitted E7 review entry in it right now; APPEND after it, do not modify existing content.

RULES: review only, no code fixes, no commits, no pushes, no em dashes or double hyphens in what you write. If docs/reviews.md write conflicts arise, re-read and append again.

If you need clarification or encounter ambiguity, output your questions in this exact format at the TOP of your response:

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: [your question with a recommended default]

Then continue with your best-effort output.

Output: verdict (PASS/FAIL), severity table, the four suite results with exact counts, E6 and E7 impact findings (fixes needed: yes/no per stream with specifics), retired-vocabulary leak scan results, and your questions.

268: /**
269:  * Every account map value must name a district that exists, and each
270:  * district must be mapped exactly account_count times, so the map and
271:  * the district table can never disagree about how many accounts live
272:  * where.
273:  */
274: function parseAccountDistrict(
275:   raw: unknown,
276:   districts: readonly DistrictRow[],
277: ): Record<string, number> {
278:   const record = asRecord(raw, 'account_district')
279:   const byDistrict = new Map(districts.map((row) => [row.district_id, row]))
280:   const mapped = new Map<number, number>()
281:   for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(record)) {
282:     if (!ACCOUNT_ID_PATTERN.test(key)) {
283:       throw new Error(`account_district key "${key}" must be an account id of digits`)
284:     }
285:     const districtId = asCount(value, `account_district["${key}"]`)
286:     if (!byDistrict.has(districtId)) {
287:       throw new Error(`account_district["${key}"] must name a district in districts, got ${districtId}`)
288:     }
289:     mapped.set(districtId, (mapped.get(districtId) ?? 0) + 1)
290:   }
291:   for (const row of districts) {
292:     const count = mapped.get(row.district_id) ?? 0
293:     if (count !== row.account_count) {
294:       throw new Error(
295:         `account_district maps ${count} accounts to district ${row.district_id}, expected districts account_count ${row.account_count}`,
296:       )
297:     }
298:   }
299:   return record as Record<string, number>
300: }

302: /**
303:  * A district split table: keys exactly the district ids, each counts
304:  * object exactly the five bands, each object summing to its district
305:  * account_count. Used for baseline and for every scenario.
306:  */
307: function parseDistrictCounts(
308:   raw: unknown,
309:   name: string,
310:   districts: readonly DistrictRow[],
311: ): Record<string, BandCounts> {
312:   const record = asRecord(raw, name)
313:   const expected = districts.map((row) => String(row.district_id))
314:   requireExactKeys(record, expected, name)
315:   const out: Record<string, BandCounts> = {}
316:   for (const key of expected) {
317:     const counts = parseBandCounts(record[key], `${name}[${key}]`)
318:     const district = districts.find((row) => String(row.district_id) === key) as DistrictRow
319:     const total = bandTotal(counts)
320:     if (total !== district.account_count) {
321:       throw new Error(
322:         `${name}[${key}] band counts sum to ${total}, expected districts account_count ${district.account_count}`,
323:       )
324:     }
325:     out[key] = counts
326:   }
327:   return out
328: }

330: function parseScenarios(
331:   raw: unknown,
332:   districts: readonly DistrictRow[],
333: ): Record<string, Record<string, BandCounts>> {

335:   const out: Record<string, Record<string, BandCounts>> = {}

406: /**
407:  * Total accounts a counts object counts: the sum of the five band
408:  * counts, used for every share this file and its callers print.
409:  */
410: export function bandTotal(counts: BandCounts): number {
411:   let total = 0
412:   for (const band of ATLAS_BAND_IDS) {
413:     total += counts[band]
414:   }
415:   return total

418: /**
419:  * District severity: the share of a district's counted accounts that
420:  * land in the critical or storm_warning bands, as a fraction from 0
421:  * to 1. This is the definition the cartogram legend prints (see
422:  * SEVERITY_DEFINITION): one number, two bands, denominator is the
423:  * district's own account total. A district with no accounts to count
424:  * reports 0, and callers must pass counts, never recompute them.
425:  */
426: export function districtSeverity(counts: BandCounts): number {
427:   const total = bandTotal(counts)
428:   if (total <= 0) {
429:     return 0
430:   }
431:   return (counts.critical + counts.storm_warning) / total
432: }

434: /** One shading bin: 0 is no severity, 4 is the heaviest. */
435: export type SeverityBin = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4

437: export interface SeverityBinSpec {
438:   bin: SeverityBin
439:   /** The verdict band whose color shades a tile in this bin. */
440:   band: VerdictBandId
441:   /** Bin range in whole percent, printed verbatim in the legend. */
442:   range: string

445: /**
446:  * Five shading bins over severity, low to high, each reusing one of
447:  * the five band colors in ladder order: a district with nothing in
448:  * the two risk bands reads Clear, the heaviest district reads
449:  * Critical. The thresholds sit low on purpose because a baseline
450:  * population spends most of its districts near zero, so a preset
451:  * twist has somewhere visible to cascade into. Bin 0 is exactly zero;
452:  * every other bin is a half open interval written as percent words.
453:  */

457:   { bin: 2, band: 'watch', range: 'over 5 to 15%' },

474:   }
475:   if (share <= 0.15) {

477:   }

480:   }

521:       districts: [...districts].sort((left, right) =>
522:         left.district_name.localeCompare(right.district_name, 'en-CA'),
523:       ),
524:     }))
525: }

109: function asArray(value: unknown, name: string): unknown[] {
110:   if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
111:     throw new Error(`${name} must be an array`)
112:   }
113:   return value
114: }

116: function asString(value: unknown, name: string): string {
117:   if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.length === 0) {
118:     throw new Error(`${name} must be a non-empty string`)
119:   }
120:   return value
121: }
122: 
123: function asInteger(value: unknown, name: string): number {
124:   if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(value)) {
125:     throw new Error(`${name} must be an integer number of accounts`)
126:   }
127:   return value
128: }
129: 
130: function asCount(value: unknown, name: string): number {
131:   const count = asInteger(value, name)
132:   if (count < 0) {
133:     throw new Error(`${name} must not be negative, got ${count}`)
134:   }
135:   return count
136: }

138: function asFiniteNumberOrNull(value: unknown, name: string): number | null {
139:   if (value === null) {
140:     return null
141:   }
142:   if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
143:     throw new Error(`${name} must be a finite number or null`)
144:   }
145:   return value
146: }

148: function asBoolean(value: unknown, name: string): boolean {
149:   if (typeof value !== 'boolean') {
150:     throw new Error(`${name} must be a boolean`)
151:   }
152:   return value
153: }
154: 
155: function asHex64(value: unknown, name: string): string {
156:   const text = asString(value, name)
157:   if (!SHA256_PATTERN.test(text)) {
158:     throw new Error(`${name} must be 64 lowercase hex digits (sha256)`)
159:   }
160:   return text
161: }

163: /** Refuse any extra or missing key so the contract cannot silently grow. */
164: function requireExactKeys(record: RawRecord, expected: readonly string[], name: string): void {
165:   const actual = Object.keys(record)
166:   const missing = expected.filter((key) => !actual.includes(key))
167:   const extra = actual.filter((key) => !expected.includes(key))
168:   if (missing.length > 0 || extra.length > 0) {
169:     const parts: string[] = []
170:     if (missing.length > 0) {
171:       parts.push(`missing ${missing.join(', ')}`)
172:     }
173:     if (extra.length > 0) {
174:       parts.push(`unexpected ${extra.join(', ')}`)
175:     }
176:     throw new Error(`${name} keys must be exactly ${expected.join(', ')} (${parts.join('; ')})`)
177:   }
178: }

180: /**
181:  * The band list key is the one spelling the loader tolerates in two
182:  * forms: verdict_bands or states. Every refusal below is written so
183:  * the message never echoes the received band names back, which keeps
184:  * retired vocabulary out of code, logs, and docs.
185:  */
186: function pickBandListKey(root: RawRecord): 'verdict_bands' | 'states' {
187:   const hasVerdictBands = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(root, 'verdict_bands')
188:   const hasStates = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(root, 'states')
189:   if (hasVerdictBands && hasStates) {
190:     throw new Error('atlas.json must carry one band list key, verdict_bands or states, not both')
191:   }
192:   if (hasVerdictBands) {
193:     return 'verdict_bands'
194:   }
195:   if (hasStates) {
196:     return 'states'
197:   }
198:   throw new Error('atlas.json is missing its band list key, verdict_bands or states')
199: }
200: 
201: function parseBandList(raw: unknown, name: string): VerdictBandId[] {
202:   const list = asArray(raw, name)
203:   if (list.length !== ATLAS_BAND_IDS.length) {
204:     throw new Error(`${name} must list the five verdict bands in ladder order`)
205:   }
206:   for (let index = 0; index < ATLAS_BAND_IDS.length; index += 1) {
207:     if (list[index] !== ATLAS_BAND_IDS[index]) {
208:       throw new Error(`${name} must list the five verdict bands in ladder order`)
209:     }
210:   }
211:   return [...ATLAS_BAND_IDS]
212: }
213: 
214: function parseBandCounts(raw: unknown, name: string): BandCounts {
215:   const record = asRecord(raw, name)
216:   requireExactKeys(record, ATLAS_BAND_IDS, name)
217:   const counts = {} as BandCounts
218:   for (const band of ATLAS_BAND_IDS) {
219:     counts[band] = asCount(record[band], `${name}.${band}`)
220:   }
221:   return counts
222: }

224: function parseSources(raw: unknown): AtlasSource[] {
225:   const sources = asArray(raw, 'sources')
226:   return sources.map((entry, index) => {
227:     const name = `sources[${index}]`
228:     const record = asRecord(entry, name)
229:     requireExactKeys(record, SOURCE_KEYS, name)
230:     const rows = asCount(record.rows, `${name}.rows`)
231:     return {
232:       path: asString(record.path, `${name}.path`),
233:       sha256: asHex64(record.sha256, `${name}.sha256`),
234:       rows,
235:     }
236:   })
237: }

239: function parseDistricts(raw: unknown): DistrictRow[] {
240:   const rows = asArray(raw, 'districts')
241:   const seen = new Set<number>()
242:   return rows.map((entry, index) => {
243:     const name = `districts[${index}]`
244:     const record = asRecord(entry, name)
245:     requireExactKeys(record, DISTRICT_KEYS, name)
246:     const districtId = asCount(record.district_id, `${name}.district_id`)
247:     if (seen.has(districtId)) {
248:       throw new Error(`${name}.district_id must be unique, got ${districtId} twice`)
249:     }
250:     seen.add(districtId)
251:     const accountCount = asCount(record.account_count, `${name}.account_count`)
252:     return {
253:       district_id: districtId,
254:       district_name: asString(record.district_name, `${name}.district_name`),
255:       region: asString(record.region, `${name}.region`),
256:       inhabitants: asCount(record.inhabitants, `${name}.inhabitants`),
257:       unemployment_rate_2023: asFiniteNumberOrNull(
258:         record.unemployment_rate_2023,
259:         `${name}.unemployment_rate_2023`,
260:       ),
261:       average_salary: asFiniteNumberOrNull(record.average_salary, `${name}.average_salary`),
262:       account_count: accountCount,
263:       no_data: asBoolean(record.no_data, `${name}.no_data`),
264:     }
265:   })
266: }

268: /**
269:  * Every account map value must name a district that exists, and each
270:  * district must be mapped exactly account_count times, so the map and
271:  * the district table can never disagree about how many accounts live
272:  * where.
273:  */
274: function parseAccountDistrict(
275:   raw: unknown,
276:   districts: readonly DistrictRow[],
277: ): Record<string, number> {
278:   const record = asRecord(raw, 'account_district')
279:   const byDistrict = new Map(districts.map((row) => [row.district_id, row]))
280:   const mapped = new Map<number, number>()
281:   for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(record)) {
282:     if (!ACCOUNT_ID_PATTERN.test(key)) {
283:       throw new Error(`account_district key "${key}" must be an account id of digits`)
284:     }
285:     const districtId = asCount(value, `account_district["${key}"]`)
286:     if (!byDistrict.has(districtId)) {
287:       throw new Error(`account_district["${key}"] must name a district in districts, got ${districtId}`)
288:     }
289:     mapped.set(districtId, (mapped.get(districtId) ?? 0) + 1)
290:   }
291:   for (const row of districts) {
292:     const count = mapped.get(row.district_id) ?? 0
293:     if (count !== row.account_count) {
294:       throw new Error(
295:         `account_district maps ${count} accounts to district ${row.district_id}, expected districts account_count ${row.account_count}`,
296:       )
297:     }
298:   }
299:   return record as Record<string, number>
300: }
301: 
302: /**
303:  * A district split table: keys exactly the district ids, each counts
304:  * object exactly the five bands, each object summing to its district
305:  * account_count. Used for baseline and for every scenario.
306:  */
307: function parseDistrictCounts(
308:   raw: unknown,
309:   name: string,
310:   districts: readonly DistrictRow[],
311: ): Record<string, BandCounts> {
312:   const record = asRecord(raw, name)
313:   const expected = districts.map((row) => String(row.district_id))
314:   requireExactKeys(record, expected, name)
315:   const out: Record<string, BandCounts> = {}
316:   for (const key of expected) {
317:     const counts = parseBandCounts(record[key], `${name}[${key}]`)
318:     const district = districts.find((row) => String(row.district_id) === key) as DistrictRow
319:     const total = bandTotal(counts)
320:     if (total !== district.account_count) {
321:       throw new Error(
322:         `${name}[${key}] band counts sum to ${total}, expected districts account_count ${district.account_count}`,
323:       )
324:     }
325:     out[key] = counts
326:   }
327:   return out
328: }
329: 
330: function parseScenarios(
331:   raw: unknown,
332:   districts: readonly DistrictRow[],
333: ): Record<string, Record<string, BandCounts>> {
334:   const record = asRecord(raw, 'scenarios')
335:   const out: Record<string, Record<string, BandCounts>> = {}
336:   for (const [presetId, value] of Object.entries(record)) {
337:     if (!PRESET_IDS.has(presetId)) {
338:       throw new Error(`scenarios key "${presetId}" is not a shipped shock preset id`)
339:     }
340:     out[presetId] = parseDistrictCounts(value, `scenarios[${presetId}]`, districts)
341:   }
342:   return out
343: }
344: 
345: /**
346:  * Validate a parsed atlas.json payload against the fixed schema and
347:  * index nothing: the artifact is already keyed the way the UI reads
348:  * it. Every refusal names the field that broke the contract.
349:  */
350: export function parseAtlasDoc(raw: unknown): AtlasDoc {
351:   const root = asRecord(raw, 'atlas.json')
352:   const bandKey = pickBandListKey(root)
353:   requireExactKeys(
354:     root,
355:     ['schema_version', 'generated_by', bandKey, 'sources', 'districts', 'account_district', 'baseline', 'scenarios'],
356:     'atlas.json',
357:   )
358: 
359:   const schemaVersion = asInteger(root.schema_version, 'schema_version')
360:   if (schemaVersion !== ATLAS_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
361:     throw new Error(
362:       `schema_version must be ${ATLAS_SCHEMA_VERSION}, got ${schemaVersion}`,
363:     )
364:   }
365: 
366:   const districts = parseDistricts(root.districts)
367:   return {
368:     schema_version: schemaVersion,
369:     generated_by: asString(root.generated_by, 'generated_by'),
370:     verdict_bands: parseBandList(root[bandKey], bandKey),
371:     sources: parseSources(root.sources),
372:     districts,
373:     account_district: parseAccountDistrict(root.account_district, districts),
374:     baseline: parseDistrictCounts(root.baseline, 'baseline', districts),
375:     scenarios: parseScenarios(root.scenarios, districts),
376:   }
377: }

379: /** Fetch and validate the bundled atlas artifact (one bundled file). */
380: export async function loadAtlas(): Promise<AtlasDoc> {
381:   const response = await fetch(`${dataBase()}data/engine/atlas.json`)
382:   if (!response.ok) {
383:     throw new Error(`atlas.json fetch failed with status ${response.status}`)
384:   }
385:   return parseAtlasDoc(await response.json())
386: }
387: 
388: /**
389:  * The bundled artifact, fetched once for the whole shell: the same
390:  * pattern as loadSharedProfiles, one request and one parse per boot
391:  * and no external network. A failed load clears the memo so the next
392:  * boot retries instead of inheriting the rejection forever.
393:  */
394: let atlasLoad: Promise<AtlasDoc> | null = null
395: 
396: export function loadSharedAtlas(): Promise<AtlasDoc> {
397:   if (!atlasLoad) {
398:     atlasLoad = loadAtlas().catch((cause: unknown) => {
399:       atlasLoad = null
400:       throw cause
401:     })
402:   }
403:   return atlasLoad
404: }

406: /**
407:  * Total accounts a counts object counts: the sum of the five band
408:  * counts, used for every share this file and its callers print.
409:  */
410: export function bandTotal(counts: BandCounts): number {
411:   let total = 0
412:   for (const band of ATLAS_BAND_IDS) {
413:     total += counts[band]
414:   }
415:   return total
416: }
417: 
418: /**
419:  * District severity: the share of a district's counted accounts that
420:  * land in the critical or storm_warning bands, as a fraction from 0
421:  * to 1. This is the definition the cartogram legend prints (see
422:  * SEVERITY_DEFINITION): one number, two bands, denominator is the
423:  * district's own account total. A district with no accounts to count
424:  * reports 0, and callers must pass counts, never recompute them.
425:  */
426: export function districtSeverity(counts: BandCounts): number {
427:   const total = bandTotal(counts)
428:   if (total <= 0) {
429:     return 0
430:   }
431:   return (counts.critical + counts.storm_warning) / total
432: }
433: 
434: /** One shading bin: 0 is no severity, 4 is the heaviest. */
435: export type SeverityBin = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
436: 
437: export interface SeverityBinSpec {
438:   bin: SeverityBin
439:   /** The verdict band whose color shades a tile in this bin. */
440:   band: VerdictBandId
441:   /** Bin range in whole percent, printed verbatim in the legend. */
442:   range: string
443: }
444: 
445: /**
446:  * Five shading bins over severity, low to high, each reusing one of
447:  * the five band colors in ladder order: a district with nothing in
448:  * the two risk bands reads Clear, the heaviest district reads
449:  * Critical. The thresholds sit low on purpose because a baseline
450:  * population spends most of its districts near zero, so a preset
451:  * twist has somewhere visible to cascade into. Bin 0 is exactly zero;
452:  * every other bin is a half open interval written as percent words.
453:  */
454: export const SEVERITY_BINS: readonly SeverityBinSpec[] = [
455:   { bin: 0, band: 'clear', range: 'exactly 0%' },
456:   { bin: 1, band: 'fair_skies', range: 'over 0 to 5%' },
457:   { bin: 2, band: 'watch', range: 'over 5 to 15%' },
458:   { bin: 3, band: 'storm_warning', range: 'over 15 to 40%' },
459:   { bin: 4, band: 'critical', range: 'over 40%' },
460: ]
461: 
462: /**
463:  * Which bin a severity share falls in. Boundaries are fractions of a
464:  * district's accounts: an exact boundary lands in the lower bin, a
465:  * non finite share reads as zero, and anything above 40 percent is
466:  * the top bin.
467:  */
468: export function binFor(share: number): SeverityBin {
469:   if (!Number.isFinite(share) || share <= 0) {
470:     return 0
471:   }
472:   if (share <= 0.05) {
473:     return 1
474:   }
475:   if (share <= 0.15) {
476:     return 2
477:   }
478:   if (share <= 0.4) {
479:     return 3
480:   }
481:   return 4
482: }
483: 
484: /** The band whose color shades a bin (never undefined for a bin). */
485: export function bandForBin(bin: SeverityBin): VerdictBandId {
486:   const spec = SEVERITY_BINS.find((entry) => entry.bin === bin)
487:   if (!spec) {
488:     throw new Error(`unknown severity bin ${bin}`)
489:   }
490:   return spec.band
491: }

493: export interface RegionGroup {
494:   region: string
495:   districts: DistrictRow[]
496: }
497: 
498: /**
499:  * Districts grouped by region: regions alphabetical, districts
500:  * alphabetical within their region. The cartogram arranges tiles by
501:  * this order and never by geography, which is exactly what its legend
502:  * says.
503:  */
504: export function regionsGrouped(doc: AtlasDoc | null | undefined): RegionGroup[] {
505:   if (!doc) {
506:     return []
507:   }
508:   const groups = new Map<string, DistrictRow[]>()
509:   for (const row of doc.districts) {
510:     const bucket = groups.get(row.region)
511:     if (bucket) {
512:       bucket.push(row)
513:     } else {
514:       groups.set(row.region, [row])
515:     }
516:   }
517:   return [...groups.entries()]
518:     .sort(([left], [right]) => left.localeCompare(right, 'en-CA'))
519:     .map(([region, districts]) => ({
520:       region,
521:       districts: [...districts].sort((left, right) =>
522:         left.district_name.localeCompare(right.district_name, 'en-CA'),
523:       ),
524:     }))
525: }

The bin ranges in SEVERITY_BINS: 0 = exactly 0%, 1 = over 0 to 5%, 2 = over 5 to 15%, 3 = over 15 to 40%, 4 = over 40%. binFor matches: share <= 0.05 → 1 ("over 0 to 5%" includes 5%? OK consistent.

Interesting details:

1. `districtScenarioFor` scenarioLabel contract: For baseline, label = liveLabel (the summary's scenarioLabel which for IDLE is presumably DEFAULT_SCENARIO_LABEL). For preset with scenario: label = liveLabel, which is the shockedAtlasScenario label. But wait: the label contract says "the summary's own label when those exact counts ran under it". For a preset, the district counts in atlas.json were precomputed by the Python side per preset. But the live summary counts are computed by TS applyTwist on the profiles. Do the precomputed district counts correspond to the same twist the live label describes? The preset twist is re-matched "field for field to the twist" via activePresetId. Hmm, but there's a subtle question: activePresetId is derived from the twist in consoleStore (recomputed atomically). The preset in atlas.json scenarios is keyed by SHOCK_PRESETS ids. 143:  * the atlas can mount before the loader resolves.

152:   const scenarioLabel = options.scenarioLabel ?? DEFAULT_SCENARIO_LABEL
153: 
154:   const counts = emptyBandCounts()
155:   for (const entry of list) {
156:     if (!entry || typeof entry !== 'object') {
157:       continue
158:     }
159:     counts[entryBand(entry)] += 1
160:   }
161: 
162:   // Total is the sum of the counts, so a defensively skipped row can
163:   // never inflate the population the percents divide by.
164:   let total = 0
165:   for (const band of ATLAS_BAND_ORDER) {
166:     total += counts[band]
167:   }
168: 
169:   const percents = emptyBandPercents()
170:   if (total > 0) {
171:     for (const band of ATLAS_BAND_ORDER) {
172:       percents[band] = roundHalfUp(counts[band] * 100, total)
173:     }
174:   }
175: 
176:   let headlineCount = 0
177:   for (const band of headlineBands) {
178:     if (ATLAS_BAND_ORDER.includes(band)) {
179:       headlineCount += counts[band]
180:     }
181:   }
182:   const headlinePercent =
183:     total > 0 && headlineCount > 0 ? roundHalfUp(headlineCount * 100, total) : 0
184:   const oneInN = headlineCount > 0 ? roundHalfUp(total, headlineCount) : null
185:   const headline = headlineSentence(
186:     total,
187:     headlineCount,
188:     headlinePercent,
189:     headlineThresholdWords,
190:     scenarioLabel,
191:   )

193:   return {
194:     total,
195:     counts,
196:     percents,
197:     headlineBands,
198:     headlineThresholdWords,

200:     headlinePercent,
201:     oneInN,
202:     headline,
203:     scenarioLabel,
204:   }
205: }
206: 
207: /**
208:  * The working sentence, word for word. Empty population reads as not
209:  * wired yet, a band that never fires reports an honest zero instead of
210:  * a ratio, and the verb swaps to "would have" the moment the numbers
211:  * ran under a twist instead of at baseline.
212:  */
213: function headlineSentence(
214:   total: number,
215:   headlineCount: number,
216:   headlinePercent: number,
217:   headlineThresholdWords: string,
218:   scenarioLabel: string,
219: ): string {
220:   if (total === 0) {

222:   }
223:   const verb = scenarioLabel === DEFAULT_SCENARIO_LABEL ? 'have' : 'would have'
224:   const threshold = `under ${headlineThresholdWords} of runway`
225:   if (headlineCount === 0) {
226:     return `No accounts ${verb} ${threshold} ${scenarioLabel}`
227:   }
228:   return `${headlinePercent}% of accounts ${verb} ${threshold} ${scenarioLabel}`
229: }
230: 
231: /**
232:  * Drill down helper: the account ids behind one band, in the order
233:  * the caller passed them. The atlas never navigates, it only reports
234:  * which ids sit in a band; the view owns what a click means.
235:  */
236: export function accountsInBand(
237:   entries: readonly AtlasEntry[] | null | undefined,
238:   band: VerdictBandId,
239: ): readonly string[] {
240:   const list = entries ?? []
241:   const ids: string[] = []
242:   for (const entry of list) {
243:     if (entry && typeof entry === 'object' && entryBand(entry) === band) {
244:       ids.push(entry.account_id)
245:     }
246:   }
247:   return ids
248: }
249: 
250: /** One scenario: the shocked rows plus the wording that describes them. */
251: export interface AtlasScenario {
252:   entries: readonly AtlasEntry[]
253:   scenarioLabel: string
254: }
255: 
256: /**
257:  * Run one twist over every profile and hand back the rows and the
258:  * wording as one object. This is the only source of scenario wording
259:  * in the atlas: the label is derived from the same twist whose
260:  * applyTwist results are in entries, so the sentence and the numbers
261:  * cannot drift apart.
262:  */
263: export function shockedAtlasScenario(
264:   profiles: readonly AccountProfile[] | null | undefined,
265:   twist: Twist,
266: ): AtlasScenario {
267:   const list = profiles ?? []
268:   const entries: AtlasEntry[] = new Array(list.length)
269:   for (let index = 0; index < list.length; index += 1) {
270:     const profile = list[index]
271:     if (!profile) {
272:       continue
273:     }
274:     const answer = applyTwist(profile, twist).runway
275:     entries[index] = {
276:       account_id: profile.account_id,
277:       runway_state: answer.state,
278:       runway_deci_months: answer.deciMonths,
279:     }
280:   }
281:   return { entries, scenarioLabel: atlasScenarioLabel(twist) }
282: }
283: 
284: /**
285:  * The wording for one twist, in priority order: untouched console
286:  * reads as baseline, a field for field preset match quotes that
287:  * preset's own label, and anything else is honestly called custom.
288:  * Deliberately not exported: prose about a scenario enters the atlas
289:  * only through shockedAtlasScenario.
290:  */
291: function atlasScenarioLabel(twist: Twist): string {
292:   if (sameTwist(twist, IDLE_TWIST)) {
293:     return DEFAULT_SCENARIO_LABEL
294:   }
295:   const normalized = normalizeTwist(twist)
296:   for (const preset of SHOCK_PRESETS) {
297:     if (sameTwist(normalizeTwist(preset.twist), normalized)) {
298:       return `under the ${preset.label.toLowerCase()} twist`
299:     }
300:   }
301:   return 'under the custom twist'
302: }

1: """Storm Atlas precompute: public/data/engine/atlas.json.
2: 
3: Called by scripts.engine.build after profiles.json lands:
4: 
5:     uv run python -m scripts.engine.build
6: 
7: The atlas document shades the 77 district cartogram tiles by verdict
8: band shares. It carries the single five band vocabulary from
9: src/lib/verdict.ts (critical, storm_warning, watch, fair_skies,
10: clear), source provenance (path, sha256, rows), every district row
11: from districts.csv joined to its account count, the account to
12: district join, and per district counts of the five bands at baseline
13: plus under each shock preset from src/lib/shockPresets.ts (layoff,
14: cost_spike, emergency_repair, combo).
15: 
16: Math contract:
17: 
18: * baseline bands map each profile's stored runway answer
19:   (runway_state plus runway_deci_months as stored in profiles.json)
20:   through band_for_runway, the port of verdictBand in
21:   src/lib/verdict.ts;
22: * scenario bands apply the same twist math as the validated Python
23:   twin in scripts/engine/shocks.py (scale_cents for the EI and bills
24:   factors, round_half_up for the one off cost, runway for the shocked
25:   answer), then band the shocked runway answer with the same helper;
26: * every district's five counts sum to its account_count, every
27:   account appears in exactly one district, and every district id in the
28:   counts exists in the districts block.
29: 
30: Determinism: no timestamps, key order fixed by sorting districts and
31: accounts numerically and by the canonical band and preset order, so
32: two consecutive builds are byte identical including atlas.json. The
33: profiles source entry records the canonical artifact path (not the
34: build output directory), which keeps tmp directory builds byte
35: identical to the shipped artifact.
36: 
37: Run from the repository root for a standalone report is not needed;
38: the build entry point owns writing. See scripts/engine/test_atlas.py
39: for the artifact contract tests.

129:     """The verdict band for one runway answer, src/lib/verdict.ts order.

160: def load_account_district(path: Path = load.ACCOUNTS_PATH) -> dict[str, int]:
161:     """account_id string to district_id int from accounts.csv.

163:     Keys are strings (the artifact key type) sorted in numeric order.
164:     One row per account is enforced loudly.
165:     """
166:     with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
167:         reader = csv.DictReader(handle)
168:         missing = [
169:             column
170:             for column in ("account_id", "district_id")
171:             if column not in (reader.fieldnames or ())
172:         ]
173:         if missing:
174:             raise load.DataError(
175:                 f"{load.rel_to_root(path)} is missing columns: "
176:                 + ", ".join(missing)
177:             )
178:         pairs: dict[str, int] = {}
179:         for row in reader:
180:             account_id = str(int(row["account_id"]))
181:             district_id = int(row["district_id"])

190: def load_districts(path: Path = DISTRICTS_PATH) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
191:     """All district rows parsed, sorted by district_id ascending.
192: 
193:     unemployment_rate_2023 and average_salary parse to float or None
194:     when the cell is empty. no_data is True when any cell of the row is
195:     missing, which is the district 69 case (its 2022 columns are
196:     empty); an incomplete district renders as "no data", never as 0.
197:     """
198:     with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
199:         reader = csv.DictReader(handle)
200:         missing = [
201:             column
202:             for column in DISTRICT_COLUMNS
203:             if column not in (reader.fieldnames or ())
204:         ]
205:         if missing:
206:             raise load.DataError(
207:                 f"{load.rel_to_root(path)} is missing columns: "
208:                 + ", ".join(missing)
209:             )
210:         rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
211:         for row in reader:
212:             no_data = any(
213:                 value is None or str(value).strip() == "" for value in row.values()
214:             )
215:             rows.append(
216:                 {
217:                     "district_id": int(row["district_id"]),
218:                     "district_name": row["district_name"],
219:                     "region": row["region"],
220:                     "inhabitants": int(row["inhabitants"]),
221:                     "unemployment_rate_2023": _float_or_none(
222:                         row["unemployment_rate_2023"]
223:                     ),
224:                     "average_salary": _float_or_none(row["average_salary"]),
225:                     "no_data": no_data,
226:                 }
227:             )
228:     rows.sort(key=lambda entry: int(entry["district_id"]))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
229:     ids = [int(entry["district_id"]) for entry in rows]

235: def _float_or_none(text: str | None) -> float | None:
236:     """Empty cell reads None, otherwise the exact float value."""

242: def shocked_band(
243:     profile: Mapping[str, object], preset: Mapping[str, int | bool]
244: ) -> str:
245:     """One profile under one preset, through the shocks.py math.
246: 
247:     Mirrors applyTwist in src/lib/shocks.ts: income scales to the EI
248:     percent only on job loss, bills delta adds to spending, the one off
249:     cost subtracts from the buffer only, and the runway runs over the
250:     shocked income and spending. The band helper then reads the shocked
251:     runway answer, so a preset only ever moves districts along the five
252:     bands.
253:     """
254:     income = int(profile["income_cents"])
255:     spending = int(profile["spending_cents"])
256:     buffer_cents = int(profile["buffer_cents"])
257:     household_bills = int(profile["household_bills_cents"])
258: 
259:     ei_pct = int(preset["ei_pct"])
260:     income_after = (
261:         int(shocks.scale_cents(income, ei_pct)) if preset["job_loss"] else income
262:     )
263:     bills_delta = int(
264:         shocks.scale_cents(household_bills, int(preset["bills_delta_pct"]))
265:     )
266:     spending_after = (
267:         spending + bills_delta + int(preset["extra_monthly_cents"])
268:     )
269:     one_off = round_half_up(spending * int(preset["one_off_tenths"]), 10)
270:     answer = shocks.runway(buffer_cents, one_off, income_after, spending_after)
271:     return band_for_runway(answer.state, answer.deci_months)

274: def count_bands(
275:     profiles: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]],
276:     account_district: Mapping[str, int],
277:     district_ids: set[int],
278:     band_of: Callable[[Mapping[str, object]], str],
279: ) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
280:     """Per district band counts for one band view of every profile."""
281:     counts: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {
282:         str(district_id): empty_counts() for district_id in sorted(district_ids)
283:     }
284:     for account_id in sorted(profiles, key=int):
285:         district_id = account_district[account_id]
286:         band = band_of(profiles[account_id])
287:         counts[str(district_id)][band] += 1
288:     return counts

291: def _check_invariants(
292:     baseline: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, int]],
293:     scenarios: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Mapping[str, int]]],
294:     district_ids: set[int],
295:     account_district: Mapping[str, int],
296: ) -> None:
297:     """Counts sum to account_count and cover exactly the district ids."""
298:     district_keys = {str(district_id) for district_id in district_ids}
299:     account_counts = Counter(account_district.values())
300:     buckets: list[tuple[str, Mapping[str, Mapping[str, int]]]] = [
301:         ("baseline", baseline),
302:         *scenarios.items(),
303:     ]
304:     for name, bucket in buckets:
305:         if set(bucket) != district_keys:
306:             raise load.DataError(
307:                 f"atlas {name}: district keys differ from districts.csv"
308:             )
309:         for district_key, counts in bucket.items():
310:             if set(counts) != set(BANDS):
311:                 raise load.DataError(
312:                     f"atlas {name} district {district_key}: band keys "
313:                     "differ from the five verdict bands"
314:                 )
315:             total = sum(counts.values())
316:             expected = account_counts[int(district_key)]
317:             if total != expected:
318:                 raise load.DataError(
319:                     f"atlas {name} district {district_key}: counts sum to "
320:                     f"{total}, expected account_count {expected}"
321:                 )
322: 
323: 
324: def build_atlas(
325:     profiles_document: Mapping[str, object], profiles_path: Path
326: ) -> dict[str, object]:
327:     """Assemble the full atlas.json document.
328: 
329:     profiles_document is the profiles.json document the build just
330:     wrote; profiles_path is that file, hashed for the sources block.
331:     Raises load.ChecksumError when a join CSV drifts from
332:     data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS and load.DataError on join violations.
333:     """
334:     load.verify_source_checksums(
335:         (load.ACCOUNTS_PATH, DISTRICTS_PATH), sums_path=load.SUMS_PATH
336:     )
337:     profiles = profiles_document["profiles"]
338:     if not isinstance(profiles, dict):
339:         raise load.DataError("profiles document has no profiles mapping")

Important observations on atlas.py:

1. `band_for_runway` matches verdictBand branch order: buffer_depleted → critical, no_shortfall → clear, then thresholds at 10, 30, 60, 120. Matches. But note TS entryBand clamps deciMonths to0..1200 before verdictBand; the Python band_for_runway doesn't clamp. Since deci comes from stored profiles.json values which the loader already enforces 0..1200, effectively equivalent. For scenario passes, shocks.runway returns deci within cap presumably. Fine.

2. `shocked_band` mirrors applyTwist. Compare with src/lib/shocks.ts applyTwist semantics: "one off subtracts from the buffer only at shocks.ts:235, billsDeltaPct adds scaleCents of H to spending at 232-234, income_after is the EI replacement only on job loss at 229-231". Here: one_off = round_half_up(spending * one_off_tenths, 10). Hmm wait: what is one_off_tenths = 10 for emergency_repair? In shockPresets.ts, the emergency repair preset presumably has oneOffCost as a fraction of spending? Let me check shockPresets.ts and shocks.ts applyTwist to verify: one_off subtracts from buffer only. Here `shocks.runway(buffer_cents, one_off, income_after, spending_after)` — runway(buffer, one_off, income, spending)? Need to see the signature: runway(buffer_cents, one_off, income, spending) presumably computes runway with one_off subtracted from buffer. Also one_off = round_half_up(spending * 10 / 10) = spending * 1? one_off_tenths: 10 means 10 tenths = 1.0 × spending? Wait "one_off_tenths": 10 for emergency_repair. If one_off = round_half_up(spending * one_off_tenths, 10) = spending * 10/10 = spending. So the emergency repair one-off cost equals one month of spending? Need to check shockPresets.ts to see the actual oneOffCost definition. Let me look at shocks.ts applyTwist and shockPresets.ts.

3. `PRESETS` comment says "test_atlas.py re parses shockPresets.ts and fails on any drift." Need to check that test.

4. `"states": list(BANDS)` — the artifact emits the band list under the `states` key! The loader accepts either verdict_bands or states. But the retired vocabulary note: the key name "states" is the older spelling. The task says loader accepts band list under verdict_bands or states key. Hmm, but the E5 coordination note says "Do not reintroduce clear/cloudy/overcast/rain/drought/storm/flood in code, artifacts, or docs" — the band list under "states" key holds the five verdict band ids, so no retired state names. The key name "states" itself is just a JSON key, not retired vocabulary (the retired names are cloudy, overcast, rain, drought, storm, flood). OK. But wait: does the shipped atlas.json use "states" or "verdict_bands"? The loader accepts both. The build emits "states". Hmm, interesting: the task brief says "src/lib/atlasData.ts strict loader (accepts band list under verdict_bands or states key)". So emitting "states" is within contract. But is it odd that the loader doc says "The band list may arrive under the verdict_bands key or the older states key name"? The Python emits states. Minor inconsistency but within contract. Actually wait, why would loader accept "verdict_bands" if build emits "states"? This is probably because an earlier version emitted verdict_bands. Not a bug.

5. 124:     billsDeltaPct, oneOffMonthsTenths. durationMonths is display only.

127:     blocks = re.findall(r"id: '([a-z_]+)'.*?twist: \{([^}]*)\}", text, re.S)
128:     parsed: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
129:     for preset_id, body in blocks:
130:         fields: dict[str, Any] = {
131:             "jobLoss": False,
132:             "incomeFactor": 0.55,
133:             "billsDeltaPct": 0,
134:             "oneOffMonthsTenths": 0,

138:                 fields[key] = True
139:             elif value == "false":
140:                 fields[key] = False
141:             elif "." in value:
142:                 fields[key] = float(value)
143:             else:
144:                 fields[key] = int(value)
145:         parsed[preset_id] = fields

The legend math tests pin the boundaries. Bin boundary semantics: binFor(0.05) = 1 ("over 0 to 5%" includes 5%), binFor(0.15) = 2 ("over 5 to 15%" includes 15%), binFor(0.4) = 3 ("over 15 to 40%" includes 40%). Legend ranges say "over 0 to 5%", "over 5 to 15%", "over 15 to 40%", "over 40%". Hmm: "over 40%" for bin 4 means strictly over 40;40% lands in bin 3 "over 15 to 40%" — the "to 40" includes 40. Consistent. "exactly 0%" for bin 0. Consistent with binFor(0)=0 and any positive → 1. But what about share = 0.0001 (0.01%)? It goes to bin 1 "over 0 to 5%" — consistent ("over 0").

The tile prints sharePercent = roundHalfUp(risky*100, total) which could round a tiny share like 0.4% to "0%" while binning it in bin 1 ("over 0 to 5%"). Tile face would read "0%" with bin 1 shading. Edge case: a district with 1 risky of 250 accounts = 0.4% → prints 0% but shades "over 0 to 5%". Slight honesty wrinkle at display rounding, but raw counts printed alongside ("1 of 250") so it's transparent. Worth a non-blocking note? The bins are computed from the exact share, the printed percent is rounded half-up. Minor. I'll note it as Info/Non-blocking.

Wait, actually check the actual district data: smallest account_count is 42 (Benesov). 1 of 42 = 2.4% → prints 2%. For0 to print0% in bin 1 you'd need risky/total < 0.005, i.e., total ≥ 200 with 1 risky. Praha has 554 accounts; 1 risky → 0.18% → prints "0%" shaded bin 1 "over 0 to 5%". Possible at baseline? Praha at baseline likely has 0 risky (bin 0). Under a twist, 1 risky of 554 → prints 0% in bin 1. The legend says bin 1 = "over 0 to 5%", the tile says "0%" — visually the tile has "1 of 554" raw counts so it's honest. Non-blocking note at most.

Now, the atlas "rain" words: RainGauge is E5's own feature name ("population rain gauge" per task), not retired vocabulary. Fine.

Now let me check test for gaugeReading rounding: "prints the whole percent, the raw fraction, and the face" — fixture:78% and 3,500 of 4,500. gaugeReading({critical+storm_warning=1000}, 4500) → outside 3500 → 77.78% → roundHalfUp → 78. Face "share of accounts outside critical and storm warning" matches the docstring "fill = share outside critical+storm_warning, 80% reference line". Good.

Now the Cartogram severity match to legend: tile prints sharePercent (risky share) and bin shading from districtSeverity. Legend prints ranges and SEVERITY_DEFINITION. Match. 

"No data hatch renders honestly (district 69 has real account data, only demographic cells missing)": Cartogram renders `no_data` flag with counts (sharePercent etc. shown), the flag says "no data", legend note says "Hatched tiles carry no demographic data; their account counts are real." Verify district 69 in the artifact has real account_count and the baseline counts include its accounts. The subagent output will confirm. Also `no_data` computed in atlas.py as "any cell of the row is missing" — for district 69, cells missing are unemployment_rate_2023/average_salary? The decisions record says "its 2022 columns are empty" and "its present 2023 values still ship as numbers under the no_data flag" — interesting: districts.csv apparently has 2022 columns too? But DISTRICT_COLUMNS only names the six. The no_data check uses `row.values()` (ALL columns from the CSV, including any2022 columns beyond DISTRICT_COLUMNS). The loader (parseDistricts) only carries the six keys. So no_data can be triggered by a missing cell in an unmapped column (2022 columns) — matches the record: district 69's 2022 columns are empty → no_data true, while its 2023 values ship as numbers. And verify.py pins no_data_ids == [69]. Consistent. But wait — maybe districts.csv has 2022 AND 2023 columns and DISTRICT_COLUMNS picks 2023; district 69 missing 2022 cells → no_data. Given the review's prior severity conventions ("test coverage gaps" are usually Low with "add tests" fix), and the E2 review rated missing tests as Low... Actually looking at prior entries: missing test coverage items were rated Low consistently. The F2 band misrender was Medium because it was factually wrong output. Here output is right but untested. I'll rate the test gap Low (with clear fix), and rate the no_data legend mismatch Medium (judge-facing claim contradicted by shipped artifact).

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the legend text: "Hatched tiles carry no demographic data; their account counts are real." Maybe "demographic data" refers to the 2022 demographic cells... 94: 
95: - **The dataset was nine relational tables, not the single CSV our pipeline assumed.** We rebuilt the ingest around `monthly_summary.csv` (the judges' actual source) and kept `transactions.csv` at 98MB out of the critical path with chunked reads.
96: - **Two implementations of one formula.** Python computes, TypeScript mirrors. Golden fixtures hand-computed in a spreadsheet keep them honest, and a verifier recomputes from raw data so drift fails the build, not the demo.

## Code Review: E5 Storm Atlas (cartogram, gauge, atlas precompute) plus E6/E7 impact check

| uv run python -m scripts.engine.verify | PASS, profiles.json sha256 9ec428bf1a78b35703aa3d36311d4ee061eac7fbd1176cfcbf111acc5c40a858, atlas invariants and dash scan clean |

### E6 impact (fixes needed: NO)
Zero references to weatherState, weather_state, stormAtlas, or atlas in judgeMode.ts, rehearsal.ts, src/components/judge, or the consoleStore key map (only the pointer comment at consoleStore.ts:27). The E6 step 0 fixes all hold (forecast.ts:33 to 35 reworded, weather.css trimmed, app.smoke.test.ts scoped to #console, atlasPlot.ts:123 comment fixed). The N key pool and edge guards interact with the atlas only through selectAccount (tracking chip and dot ring); scenario routing keys on twist plus activePresetId, which matchPreset recomputes atomically (consoleStore.ts:108, 226, 305), so nothing can desync the tiles. judge-sheet.html:289 speaks the five verdict bands.

### E7 impact (fixes needed: NO on E7; one E5 side gap)
receipts.ts and atlasData.ts do not collide (import.meta.glob eager over public/data/memo-devnet*.json at receipts.ts:110 to 113 versus one fetch of data/engine/atlas.json at atlasData.ts:381; disjoint files and mechanisms). BaselineCard's ReceiptStamp (BaselineCard.tsx:4, 107) breaks no E5 or console test (589 of 589 green). The uncommitted E7 set is internally consistent: all three public/data/memo-devnet*.json plus scripts/solana/evidence siblings present, ReceiptStamp pair present, receipts.test.ts digest pins read present findings.json and model_card.json, index.css receipt block contiguous at 2591 to 2634, dashScan covers the receipts pair and (via console AUTO_DIRS) the stamp pair. The one gap found is the E5 side dashScan registration of the atlasData files above.

### Retired-vocabulary leak scan
Only one live leak: docs/devpost.md:87 to 88, 131 (the Medium above). public/data/engine/atlas.json carries the five band ids and zero retired names. Allowed or dead only: index.css:1263 to 1365 --rv-drought Money River tokens and the BalanceRiver drought metaphor (pre pivot, per your note), docs/research.md tables, the historical E5 records at docs/decisions.md:431 to 519 that the correction entry preserves, AGENTS.md's coordination note, one plain verb at scripts/ingest/probe_schema.py:798, and a stale unreachable scripts/engine/__pycache__/weather_state.cpython-314.pyc (harmless clutter). docs/architecture.md:34 and src/lib/forecast.ts:34 mention the ladder only to record its deletion. The AGENTS.md coordination items themselves are satisfied: weather_state.py and goldens deleted, verify.py ladder assertions replaced by the five band check with the profiles gate untouched, correction entry filed at docs/decisions.md:482 to 519, cartogram kept on the five bands.
